domain_restrictions: a, b, and r are integers
q is a formal indeterminate, not a specialized numeric value
n ranges over nonnegative integers in the product definition
D is nonnegative because r >= 0 and b - a >= 0
j is an integer with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2)
R is assumed to be a polynomial with integer coefficients
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Under the integer constraints 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, if the quotient defining R is actually a polynomial with integer coefficients, then every coefficient of q to the power j in R is a nonnegative integer for all integers j from 0 through floor(r times (b - a) divided by 2).
quantifier_order: For all integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0
For each nonnegative integer n, define the q-factorial quantity
Define R from a, b, r, and q by the stated quotient
Define D as r times (b - a)
Assume the resulting R is an element of Z[q]
For every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient condition is asserted

variables.name: q
variables.role: symbol used to form q-factorials and the polynomial R

variables.name: n
variables.role: index in the finite product defining the q-factorial

variables.domain: integer polynomials in q, assumed to lie in Z[q]
variables.name: R
variables.role: defined quantity from a, b, r, and q

variables.name: D
variables.role: derived quantity equal to r times (b - a)

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are introduced; the statement is universally quantified after the definitions and the assumption that R is a polynomial.

statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.
